incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored espionage (Ministry of State Security)
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of a Sqgame Android card-game update package, since at least November 2024, that delivered the BirdCall backdoor when victims sideloaded the games outside the Play Store.
incidents.impact: ESET attributes the operation to APT37 and says BirdCall harvests SMS, contacts, call logs, media files, screenshots and audio from compromised phones, with seven Android variants developed over several months. The campaign appears aimed at North Korean defectors and refugees in the border region.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Long-running intrusions deploying multiple custom malware families (NetDraft, an updated CloudSorcerer, VSHELL/SNOWLIGHT and a new Rust stager 'SNOWRUST') alongside Impacket, PowerShell recon and AD database extraction.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos disclosed UAT-8302, a China-nexus APT cluster targeting government networks since late 2024 (South America) and into 2025 (southeastern Europe). Toolset overlaps with several previously reported China-linked clusters and is consistent with long-term persistent access for intelligence collection.

incidents.vector: Fake ScreenConnect updater drops a Rust loader that stages an obfuscated .NET RAT (CloudZ); a custom 'Pheno' plugin abuses the Microsoft Phone Link SQLite database to siphon synced SMS messages, including SMS-based one-time passwords, without touching the phone itself.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos identified an intrusion active since at least January 2026 in which CloudZ exfiltrates browser credentials and intercepts Phone Link data to defeat SMS-based MFA. The operator uses Pastebin and Cloudflare Workers to rotate C2 configuration and hide traffic among legitimate browser requests.

incidents.victim: Industrial, consulting, retail and transportation organisations in India and Russia
incidents.vector: Tax-themed phishing emails impersonating Indian and Russian tax authorities deliver a modified Rust loader (RustSL) that drops the ValleyRAT backdoor and a previously undocumented Python backdoor (ABCDoor) hiding under pythonw.exe.
incidents.impact: Kaspersky logged more than 1,600 malicious messages between January and February 2026. ABCDoor offers screen streaming, remote keyboard and mouse control, clipboard theft, file operations and limited encryption. The campaign is the China-linked group's first observed expansion into Russian targets, alongside ongoing Indian targeting.

incidents.vector: Unauthorised access to Instructure systems was discovered Friday night; ShinyHunters claimed responsibility two days later. Initial access vector has not been disclosed; containment included revoking privileged credentials and access tokens.
incidents.impact: Hackers accessed names, email addresses, student IDs and user-to-user messages at unspecified educational institutions. The group claims 3.6 TB of data covering more than 9,000 schools. Instructure says no passwords, financial information or government documents were taken.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed access path into a portion of Trellix's source code repository.
incidents.impact: Trellix disclosed a threat actor gained unauthorised access to part of its source code. The company says it has found no evidence the source-code release or distribution process was affected, but source-code visibility could expose detection logic and control placement to attackers. Investigation continues with outside forensics support.

incidents.vector: Attacker allegedly compromised an admin account on Wasabi Protocol and reduced the delay on admin actions to zero, allowing instant malicious transactions across the platform's multi-chain integration.
incidents.impact: Approximately $5 million in crypto assets stolen via cross-chain integrations, joining a string of DeFi heists in recent weeks.

incidents.vector: Data-theft extortion attack by World Leaks (a rebrand of Hunters International); intrusion details have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: World Leaks published roughly 8.5 TB of allegedly stolen files including payroll, contracts, financial statements and editorial communications. Independent outlets reported the leaked notes contain a January 2025 editorial-meeting reference to 'contacting Moscow for help' on anti-Zelensky coverage. Mediaworks confirmed the breach and is pursuing legal action against outlets that report on the leak.

incidents.vector: Volumetric distributed denial-of-service against Ubuntu/Canonical web infrastructure and APIs, claimed by a hacktivist group calling itself the 313 Team.
incidents.impact: DDoS over Thursday and Friday took down most Ubuntu/Canonical web properties, preventing users from installing or updating Ubuntu systems. The same group claimed previous attacks on Bluesky and Mastodon.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into Moldova's national healthcare database; specific entry vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Moldovan officials confirmed sensitive data was stolen from CNAM, which holds personal and financial details on virtually every adult resident plus financials on contracted private medical providers. Around 30% of agency data was reportedly impacted (stolen and/or restored from backup). No ransom demand was made; the cybersecurity agency did not rule out Russian involvement amid heightened Moscow-Chișinău tensions.

incidents.vector: Mirai-variant botnet built on TP-Link Archer AX21 routers vulnerable to CVE-2023-1389 plus open DNS resolvers used for amplification. Attack scripts were keyed to private SSH credentials and Huge Networks IP space.
incidents.impact: An exposed file archive showed an extended campaign of large DDoS attacks against small Brazilian ISPs, run from infrastructure tied to Brazilian DDoS-mitigation provider Huge Networks. The CEO blames a January intrusion of two dev servers and his personal SSH keys; investigators are still tracing the operator. Each prefix was hit for 10–60 seconds at a time.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Microsoft Exchange email server at the embassy, part of a broader campaign that hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers this year.
incidents.impact: Chinese hackers stole Cuban diplomats' email inboxes to gather intelligence on the U.S. naval blockade of Cuba, per Bloomberg reporting cited by industry trackers.

incidents.victim: Linux systems globally (Ubuntu, RHEL, SUSE, Debian, AlmaLinux, Amazon Linux)
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-31431 'Copy Fail' — a deterministic logic flaw in the Linux kernel algif_aead AEAD module lets a local unprivileged user write four controlled bytes into the kernel page cache of setuid binaries (su, sudo) for instant root, without race conditions.
incidents.impact: Researchers disclosed the bug on April 29 with a 732-byte Python PoC that works unmodified across most mainstream distros built since 2017. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on May 1; researchers report active in-the-wild exploitation. The flaw enables Kubernetes container escapes and CI/CD pipeline takeover.

incidents.victim: Web hosting providers and cPanel-managed sites (incl. Guam government)
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-41940, an authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8) affecting all supported versions of cPanel/WHM/WP Squared. PoC and patch-diff appeared within a day, spawning Mirai botnet payloads, a '.sorry'-extension ransomware, fake-extortion defacements demanding $8,000 in BTC, and worming behaviour.
incidents.impact: Censys logged ~15,000 potentially compromised cPanel instances within 24 hours; Shadowserver later put the figure at more than 44,000 systems. KnownHost and others observed in-the-wild exploitation as far back as Feb 23, before disclosure. Defaced victims include several Guam government websites. The flaw sits on management ports of infrastructure powering ~70 million domains.

incidents.vector: Email-bombing followed by Microsoft Teams chat from a fake IT helpdesk persona; victim was lured to install a 'Mailbox Repair Utility' that dropped an AutoHotKey loader, a malicious Edge browser extension (SNOWBELT), and tunnelling implants (SNOWGLAZE/SNOWBASIN). LSASS memory was exfiltrated via LimeWire and pass-the-hash used to reach the domain controller.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group disclosed UNC6692, a multi-stage intrusion that achieved deep network compromise including extraction of NTDS.dit, SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives via FTK Imager and screen-capture of Domain Administrator activity, all while exfiltrating data through attacker-controlled AWS S3 buckets.

incidents.victim: U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies (Cisco ASA / Firepower / Secure Firewall users)
incidents.vector: Advanced persistent threat actor exploited Cisco ASA flaws CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362 to install FIRESTARTER, a remote-access implant that survives firmware patching on Cisco ASA, Firepower 1000/2100/4100/9300 and Secure Firewall 1200/3100/4200 series.
incidents.impact: CISA, in a malware analysis report co-sealed with NCSC-UK, said proactive monitoring of FCEB Cisco devices uncovered live FIRESTARTER infections and that simply patching firmware does not remove the actor. CISA Emergency Directive 25-03 was updated, requiring federal agencies to identify in-scope appliances, generate forensic data and apply new vendor updates. ACSC issued a parallel high alert.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Signal account belonging to the Bundestag President; part of a broader Russia-attributed Signal/WhatsApp targeting campaign flagged by Germany's cybersecurity agency earlier in the year.
incidents.impact: Russian cyber spies gained access to a sensitive Signal group chat that included Chancellor Friedrich Merz, allowing the actor to read messages from senior German leadership. Merz's own account was not compromised. (Der Spiegel reporting.)

incidents.industry: Healthcare, financial services, professional services, technology
incidents.vector: Multi-wave phishing impersonating internal compliance teams ('Internal Regulatory COC', 'Workforce Communications'), with PDF attachments linking through Cloudflare CAPTCHAs and intermediate sites to a 'Sign in with Microsoft' adversary-in-the-middle proxy that captures live authentication tokens.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Defender Research observed more than 35,000 targeted users between April 14 and 16. AiTM token theft bypasses non-phishing-resistant MFA, granting immediate account access; campaign infrastructure used likely cloud-hosted Windows VMs and attacker-controlled .de domains.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering attack against DigiCert tech support: an attacker posing as a customer convinced two staffers to run a malicious Windows screensaver (.SCR) file. On one workstation a misconfigured CrowdStrike EDR agent (disconnected from its management server) failed to alert, giving the actor nearly two weeks of access.
incidents.impact: Attacker stole 'initialization codes' for in-flight EV code-signing orders, then obtained 27 EV code-signing certificates across multiple customer accounts. The certificates were used to sign payloads delivering Zhong Stealer, a malware family historically tied to a Chinese e-crime cluster. DigiCert revoked all 60 affected certificates after a third-party researcher reported the abuse.

incidents.vector: Hijack of a foreign-debt repayment workflow; the precise compromise method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Approximately $2.5 million scheduled for debt repayment to Australia was diverted by attackers. Sri Lanka has requested investigative help from Australian law enforcement.
